comments.name: Martin Gburík
comments.content:
the programming of the validation is so great, but from the UX view it's not a very good approach.
This great article (link bellow) about forms UX says:
But inline validation should be implemented carefully:
- Avoid showing inline validation on focus.
- Don’t validate after each character typed.

I recommend for everyone to read it.
https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2018/08/best-practices-for-mobile-form-design/

comments.name: PieEatingNinjas
comments.content:
Hi Martin! Thanks for your feedback, much appreciated!
I'm not at all a UX expert, so I've put the link you've share on my to-read list.
In my defense, like I've said at the beginning of my post, I'm not pretending that this is the best way of dealing with data validation and it has proven in my projects to be a good solution (both from a developer and user point of view). 
And that's why I really appreciate your feedback, I'll be taking it into account when setting up a new project which requires data validation.
